name: Saint-Emilion

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Malbec sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
One of the two regional appellations allowed anywhere in Bordeaux, beside plain Bordeaux. Together they cover about half the Bordeaux vineyard.

In 1855 brokers ranked Bordeaux estates by reputation and price. Reds were ranked from first to fifth growths, nearly all in the Médoc, and the sweet whites of Sauternes and Barsac from superior first growth to second growth.
Saint-Émilion's own classification, first published in 1955 and revised since. Plain Saint-Émilion Grand Cru is an appellation, not part of this ranking.
keyfacts: The Saint-Émilion classification dates from 1955, covers wines of the Saint-Émilion Grand Cru appellation, and is updated every 10 years or so.
The classification has three levels: Premier grand cru classé A, Premier grand cru classé B, and Grand cru classé.
As of the 2022 classification, Château Figeac and Château Pavie are the two estates at the highest level.
Merlot is by far the main grape, with Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon the other principal varieties.
The appellation lies east of Libourne on a limestone plateau above the Dordogne, and its vineyard covered about 13,600 acres in 2010.

notes: Right Bank reds, around Libourne, are led by Merlot with very little Cabernet Sauvignon.
They often have great fruit concentration and softer tannins, and they live long.

blurb.text: A Right Bank Bordeaux appellation for red wine, around the town of Saint-Émilion just east of Libourne, above the Dordogne. Its wines are made mainly from Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon. Its vineyard landscape was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.
